notes: Pi header pins use physical pin numbers: GND=6, GPIO15=10, GPIO25=22, GPIO8=24, GPIO7=26, GPIO21=40. In the diagram the left column holds the odd pins and the right column the even pins.
The ground rail is the right-hand rail strip next to the red line. It is named bp.N here. The rail naming and the row numbers used for the rail holes are approximate, and the whole rail is one strip.

Each LED has a 330R resistor between its GPIO wire and its anode, on the anode side. The resistor is on columns e (top half) and h (bottom half), and the LED anode is in column j. The cathode goes to the ground rail.
The buzzer + (pin 2) is on the GPIO15 row (4b.g strip). Its other leg (pin 1) goes to the ground rail.

The button sits across the centre gap. Row 28 is one side, wired to ground. Row 30 is the other side, wired to GPIO21. Pressing joins the two rows, so the 28/30 legs are on different sides of the switch.
The Pi pin side of each wire is end a and the breadboard side is end b, except wire7, which is breadboard to rail.
The diagram labels a + rail but the text says to use it as ground, so it is wired to ground.
